slides.title: Cover Slide/Main Slide
slides.speaker: Aryanraj S Singh
slides.script: “We are Team 10. We study whether Differential Evolution can improve the training recipe of an EfficientNet-B0 tomato classifier. We built the optimizer, the evaluation pipeline, and an offline interface for inspecting predictions and search behavior. Our guide is Manoj Kumar S, Assistant Professor.”

slides.title: Introduction to Optimization Problems
slides.speaker: Aryanraj S Singh
slides.script: “An optimization problem has decisions, an objective, and constraints. Our decisions include learning rate, regularization, head width, and fine-tuning depth. The objective is validation macro-F1. A candidate costs an actual training run, and this mixed recipe cannot be optimized directly by differentiating the validation score.”

slides.title: What are Nature-Inspired Algorithms?
slides.speaker: Aryanraj S Singh
slides.script: “A population maintains several possible solutions. Variation explores new recipes, while selection retains useful ones. Exploration seeks new regions and exploitation refines promising ones. DE uses numerical differences between candidates to propose steps. Its operators are inspectable, but it does not guarantee a global optimum.”

slides.title: Classification of Nature-Inspired Algorithms
slides.speaker: Aryanraj S Singh
slides.script:
“GA, DE, and evolution strategies are evolutionary methods. PSO, ACO, and ABC are swarm methods. Simulated annealing uses a physics analogy; BBO uses biogeography. Categories overlap. We judge mechanisms and measured behavior, not the metaphor. In particular, binomial crossover makes the full DE algorithm coordinate-dependent.”

Handoff: “Richik will explain the data and the baseline fixed before search.”

slides.title: Problem Statement
slides.speaker: Richik Chaudhuri
slides.script: “The fixed application is the color tomato subset of PlantVillage. The cleaned count on the slide comes from the preparation output. Exact duplicates are removed and perceptually similar groups stay in one split. These controlled leaf images support reproducible evaluation, but they do not establish performance on arbitrary field photographs.”

slides.title: Implementation and Results (1/10)
slides.speaker: Richik Chaudhuri
slides.script:
“Follow the pipeline from verified images to the fixed baseline, DE and random search, validation reranking, repeated final training, and the locked test. Both searches use equal candidate budgets and the same proxy conditions. Final recipes are frozen before test evaluation. The demo loads the exact seed-zero checkpoints.”

Point to the baseline path and the separate reranking paths. Do not imply that the baseline is selected by reranking.

slides.title: Implementation and Results (2/10)
slides.speaker: Richik Chaudhuri
slides.script:
“The baseline freezes EfficientNet-B0 and trains a 256-unit head with dropout 0.2, Adam at 0.001, and no weight decay or label smoothing. It uses the common crop-and-flip pipeline without extra RandAugment. Candidate recipes use AdamW. Therefore, the baseline comparison concerns the whole recipe; DE versus random search more directly compares proposal strategies.”

Handoff: “Suraj will explain the operators and the seven decisions they evolve.”

slides.title: Implementation and Results (3/10)
slides.speaker: Suraj B
slides.script:
“For each target, choose three distinct donors, all excluding that target. Mutation adds F times a donor difference to the third donor. Repair an out-of-range coordinate between its parent and violated bound. Binomial crossover takes mutant coordinates with probability CR and forces at least one mutant coordinate. Selection accepts an equal or better validation score.”

Point to the operator example. “We test these invariants directly. Each completed evaluation persists the population and random-generator state so an interrupted run can resume.”

slides.title: Implementation and Results (4/10)
slides.speaker: Suraj B
slides.script:
“All seven genes lie between zero and one. Learning rate and weight decay decode logarithmically; head width, unfreezing depth, and augmentation are discrete. A zero-width head is a direct linear classifier. Augmentation zero disables extra RandAugment, retaining the common crop-and-flip transforms. Population, F, CR, and the evaluation budget are fixed before search.”

Point to the two logarithmic rows and the printed budget; avoid reading every bound aloud.

slides.title: Implementation and Results (5/10)
slides.speaker: Suraj B
slides.script:
“This is proxy validation macro-F1 against candidate evaluations. Both searches use a fresh pretrained model, a shared training seed, and the same fixed subset. Their top three distinct recipes are reranked at full resolution using validation only. Discuss the actual curves, including random-search advantages or ties; a proxy winner need not be the final test winner.”

If search is still running: “This is a partial search trace. The planned budget and final comparison are not complete.”

slides.title: Implementation and Results (6/10)
slides.speaker: Suraj B
slides.script:
“The displayed means and standard deviations cover all three registered training seeds. Compare baseline and DE accuracy and macro-F1, then relate them to the random-search control in the full results. Relative error reduction is signed: a negative value means more error. We do not substitute the best seed or a search score.”

Read the current values and state the observed direction. Do not invent a winner or significance claim. If the final artifact is absent, say: “These held-out results remain pending.”

Handoff: “Sushant will show where the models succeed, fail, and disagree.”

slides.title: Implementation and Results (7/10)
slides.speaker: Sushant Deo
slides.script: “The confusion matrices have identical normalized scales. Rows show true classes; off-diagonal cells show mistakes. Point to the largest measured confusion and compare the same cells between models. Similar symptoms may be relevant, but a biological explanation requires image inspection and expertise. We do not assume a particular class pair will dominate.”

slides.title: Implementation and Results (8/10)
slides.speaker: Sushant Deo
slides.script:
“These per-class F1 values average all registered seeds and are ordered by measured DE-minus-baseline change. Read the strongest gain and any regression or remaining weakness. Macro-F1 gives every class equal weight, which matters for this imbalanced dataset.”

If final class metrics are absent, identify this as a pending analysis instead of choosing example winners.

slides.title: Implementation and Results (9/10)
slides.speaker: Sushant Deo
slides.script:
“Grad-CAM uses gradients at the last convolution to highlight evidence for the predicted class. Compare the same leaf, the labels, and both maps. A heatmap is not a lesion mask or causal proof, and its intensity is not a calibrated confidence score.”

Point to one actual displayed case. Describe only visible evidence; do not infer a biological explanation from the colors alone.

slides.title: Implementation and Results (10/10)
slides.speaker: Sushant Deo
slides.script:
“Both models see identical blur, noise, illumination, JPEG, and low-light corruptions at three severities. Read the actual trend and identify where either model remains sensitive. These controlled probes test selected disturbances; they do not replace independently collected field images.”

If final corruption metrics are unavailable, identify this analysis as pending. Do not predict a robustness advantage.

slides.title: Live Demo
slides.speaker: Sushant Deo
slides.script:
First 25 seconds: Open the local demo, press P if needed, select an included leaf, and analyze it. Point to both predictions, top-three probabilities, and the Grad-CAM maps that appear automatically. Probabilities apply to the known tomato classes.

Next 15 seconds: Apply mild blur and analyze again. Describe the actual change in scores without promising that DE improves this particular example.

Final 20 seconds: Open Evolution Lab, select Rastrigin, run, pause with Space, and inspect the timeline. Explain the population points and objective. Distinguish this mathematical search from replaying the separate CNN experiment. Return to the slides.

If a checkpoint is unavailable or analysis fails, acknowledge the state. Use demo/demo.gif only as an identified recording, never as a substitute claimed to be live inference.

slides.title: Performance Metrics and Benchmarking (1/5)
slides.speaker: Sushant Deo
slides.script: “Accuracy counts correct labels. Precision, recall, and F1 are calculated per class and macro-averaged. ROC-AUC measures ranking. Calibration asks whether confidence matches correctness, and latency measures the specified forward pass. These metrics answer different questions; none alone proves readiness for field deployment.”

slides.title: Performance Metrics and Benchmarking (2/5)
slides.speaker: Sushant Deo
slides.script:
“These confidence intervals use one thousand deterministic bootstrap resamples of seed-zero predictions. They describe resampling uncertainty on this split, not differences across farms. Exact two-sided McNemar compares paired correctness on the same images. Read its disagreement counts and p-value; statistical significance is not effect size. Three-seed variation was reported separately.”

If evaluation is unfinished, the intervals and paired test remain pending. Do not replace them with training or validation variation.

Handoff: “Richik will separate optimizer validation from classifier evaluation and explain the computational cost.”

slides.title: Performance Metrics and Benchmarking (3/5)
slides.speaker: Richik Chaudhuri
slides.script:
“The completed analytic study uses Sphere, Rosenbrock, Rastrigin, Ackley, and Griewank. DE, jDE, GA, PSO, and random search receive equal function-evaluation budgets across all registered seeds. Curves show median best-so-far error with interquartile spread. This tests the optimizer independently of the expensive CNN objective.”

Point to the budget and dimension printed on the slide. The two-dimensional landscapes in the demo are explanatory; the main quantitative study is ten-dimensional.

slides.title: Performance Metrics and Benchmarking (4/5)
slides.speaker: Richik Chaudhuri
slides.script:
“Lower final error is better. DE has the lowest median on Rosenbrock; PSO on Sphere and Ackley; jDE on Rastrigin and Griewank. This is landscape-dependent evidence, not a universal ranking. The report also shows mean, standard deviation, best runs, and exploratory rank-sum outputs.”

If asked about those tests: “They are unadjusted for multiple comparisons and not tie-corrected, despite some ties. We do not treat their approximate p-values as confirmatory significance evidence.”

slides.title: Performance Metrics and Benchmarking (5/5)
slides.speaker: Richik Chaudhuri
slides.script:
“Training time sums all three final seeds. Search time sums uncached candidate-training durations; it is not exclusive wall-clock use. Inference is a warmed batch-one forward pass on the recorded device. The local demo also decodes images and computes Grad-CAM on CPU, so its complete response time is a different measurement.”

Read the table only after final costs exist. Keep completed mathematical-benchmark time separate from unfinished CNN training costs.

slides.title: Advantages and Limitations
slides.speaker: Aryanraj S Singh
slides.script: “Our strengths are auditable operators, documented splits, equal budgets, resumable execution, and offline inference. Limitations include controlled imagery, one crop and split, proxy noise, and training cost. We ran one CNN search per method. Repeated final seeds measure training variation for selected recipes, not variation across independent searches. Negative results remain visible.”

slides.title: Future Scope
slides.speaker: Suraj B
slides.script: “Next studies should evaluate real field images, validate unknown-input handling, and balance predictive quality with latency. Adaptive DE, multi-fidelity allocation, on-device export, and expert feedback are promising extensions. These require fresh evaluation protocols; they are proposed work, not completed claims.”
